items.headline: High Wind Warning issued September 10 at 1:54AM AKDT until September 11 at 4:00PM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
items.description:
* WHAT...Southwest winds 30 to 45 mph with gusts up to 60 mph
expected.

* WHERE...Bering Strait Coast, Diomede, and St Lawrence Island.

* WHEN...Until 4 PM AKDT Friday.

* IMPACTS...High winds may move loose debris, blow around unsecured
objects, damage property, and cause power outages. Travel could be
difficult.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Winds peak near St. Lawrence Island Thursday
morning and through the Bering Strait Thursday through Friday
morning.

items.headline: Hydrologic Outlook issued September 9 at 3:51PM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
items.description:
ESFAFC

Hydrologic Concerns:
* High water flowing down the Kuskokwim River, in combination with
storm surge pushing up the up river, could cause water levels to
rise between bankfull and minor flood stage.
* The highest water levels would occur if the downstream high water
flow, storm surge, and high tide all occurred simultaneously.

Potential Impacts:
* More likely scenario: Bankfull conditions with no flooding
expected.
* Worst case scenario: Nuisance flooding in low-lying areas.

items.headline: Hydrologic Outlook issued September 9 at 1:51PM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
items.description:
ESFAFG

...Locations Impacted...
Streams draining southern slopes of the Western Brooks Range.

Incoming rainfall from a atmospheric river will bring rainfall to the
southern slopes of the western end of the Brooks Range through
Friday.  Rainfall totals may exceed two inches in some locations and
cause significant rises on small streams.

The Kobuk, Noatak, and Wulik Rivers should also see rises from this
system into the weekend, but no flooding is expected.
